_comment: Solver core for a browser-side solver of the Gonzalez et al. (2025) model, exported from the Python reference (src/export_solver_core.py). Floats are unrounded: Python's shortest repr, which JSON.parse reads back to the identical double. Rupee figures are an FX conversion of the paper's US$ cost parameters. Check it against the Python code with scripts/verify_js_fixtures.py.

decoder_spec._comment: How decoder.decode() turns (pop, mask) into costs, step by step and in the exact floating-point order needed to reproduce it bit for bit. Indices: points 0..nI-1; matrix C row/col 0 is the depot and point i is row/col i+1; days 0..n_days-1 (0 = MON); mask/pop columns are the working days in work_days order.
decoder_spec.chromosome: pop[i][c] = position of point i in working day c's visiting order (a permutation of 0..nI-1); mask[i][c] = 1 if point i is collected on working day c.
decoder_spec.1_accumulation: visited[i][t] = (mask[i][c] == 1) for t = work_days[c], false on rest days. carry = W (points only, W[1..nI]). Repeat up to 50 times: prev = copy(carry); for t in 0..n_days-1, for each i: w[i][t] = W[i] + carry[i]; carry[i] = visited[i][t] ? 0 : w[i][t]. Stop when for every i: carry[i] == prev[i] or |carry[i] - prev[i]| <= 1e-12 + 1e-5 * |prev[i]| (np.allclose defaults). wmax[i] = max over t of w[i][t].
decoder_spec.2_bins: n_visits[i] = sum of mask[i][*] (as a float). For each bin b in order: fits = cap[b] >= wmax[i] - 1e-9; cost = bin_cost[b] + (ccv * service[b]) * n_visits[i] if fits else +Infinity. Choose the first b with the strictly smallest cost (ties -> lowest b). If the smallest is Infinity, the solution is invalid (no bin fits).
decoder_spec.3_routes: For each working day in order: the points with mask 1, sorted by pop value ascending (stable: ties keep ascending point index). Walk them with load = 0: if the route is non-empty and load + w[i][day] > Q + 1e-9, close the route and start a new one (load = 0). Then load += w[i][day] and append i.
decoder_spec.4_duration: travel = C[0][s0+1], then travel += C[s_k+1][s_k+1+1] for each consecutive pair in order, then travel += C[s_last+1][0]. service = pairwise_sum([service[bins[s]] for s in route]). duration = (travel + service) + tu.
decoder_spec.pairwise_sum: NumPy's float64 sum of a[0..n-1]: result = 0.0 + block(a). For n < 8: r = -0.0; r += a[k] for k in order. For 8 <= n <= 128: r0..r7 = a[0..7]; for i = 8 step 8 while i < n - n%8: r0 += a[i], ..., r7 += a[i+7]; res = ((r0+r1)+(r2+r3))+((r4+r5)+(r6+r7)); then res += a[i] for the remaining i. For n > 128: n2 = floor(n/2) - (floor(n/2) % 8); block(a[0:n2]) + block(a[n2:n]) recursively.
decoder_spec.5_costs: bin_cost = pairwise_sum([bin_cost[bins[i]] for i in 0..nI-1]). total_minutes = 0.0; total_minutes += duration for each route in order (days ascending, routes in creation order). routing_cost = ccv * total_minutes. overall_cost = bin_cost + routing_cost.
decoder_spec.6_penalty: penalty = 0.0. For day in 0..n_days-1: if the day has n_routes > n_vehicles: penalty += lam * (n_routes - n_vehicles) / n_vehicles. Then for each route in order: if duration > TL + 1e-9: penalty += gamma * (duration - TL). feasible = (penalty == 0). fitness = overall_cost + penalty (what SA and GA minimise).

paper_expected._comment: Gonzalez et al. (2025), Appendix A, Tables 16-17, as published (2 decimals). Points are 1-based here, as in the paper; days 0 = MON.

parity._comment: 50 random (pop, mask) pairs per instance (optimizers.random_solution, repaired masks) with the exact Python decode, penalties at the instance's lam/gamma. Stops are 0-based points.

parity_feasible._comment: Random schedules on these instances are all infeasible (they break TL or the fleet size), so these are the saved best solutions of the 30 SA and 30 GA runs per instance (all feasible, penalty 0), with the same exact Python decode.
